items.title: Keyboard-only critical workflow
evidence: 2026-09-05: User completed the real production critical workflow without a pointing device. Forward Tab/Space/Enter navigation worked across primary sections; player detail opened with Enter and closed with Esc without losing usable focus; League Setup destructive/disconnect confirmation was reachable and cancellable entirely by keyboard; Shift+Tab reverse navigation remained visible and predictable.
items.notes: Keyboard-only production workflow passed for the tested Chrome/Windows session.

items.title: Screen-reader critical workflow
items.notes: Run the critical workflow with NVDA, VoiceOver, or an equivalent assistive technology and record browser/AT versions plus any defects.

items.title: Real browser 200 percent zoom
evidence: 2026-09-05: User ran the deployed site at actual Chrome 200% zoom on a 1920x1050 desktop and reported the interface felt too large. Video review shows the desktop sidebar remains permanently expanded at the effective narrow CSS viewport while the topbar controls stay desktop-style; multiple page titles wrap into two or three lines and primary content is squeezed into a narrow column. No clear overlap or horizontal page overflow was observed in the recording, but the reflow quality is not acceptable enough to mark this field check passed. Responsive breakpoint/refinement required, followed by real 200% retest.

2026-09-05: v0.9.75 candidate adds a compact-desktop reflow specifically for 721-1000 CSS-pixel viewports so a 1920px desktop at 200% Chrome zoom uses off-canvas navigation and a two-row header instead of retaining the full desktop sidebar. Automated readiness coverage now includes the observed 960 CSS-pixel field case plus the existing 720 CSS-pixel 200%-equivalent case. Real deployed 200% zoom retest is still required before this item can pass.

2026-09-05: User retested deployed v0.9.76 at actual Chrome 200% zoom. The compact reflow was materially improved across Overview, Lineup Lab, Waivers, Player Alerts, What Changed, and Season Plan, with no reported horizontal overflow and the prior Waivers/Season Plan navigation lag gone. However, the off-canvas left navigation could not be scrolled far enough to reach League Setup on the short effective viewport, so the field check remains pending.

2026-09-05: v0.9.77 candidate makes the sidebar navigation its own vertical scroll region while keeping the brand and source status stable. The readiness audit now reproduces the real 1920x1050-at-200% dimensions as a 960x525 CSS-pixel viewport, verifies scrollability when navigation content overflows, brings League Setup into view, and activates it. Real deployed retest is still required before this item can pass.

2026-09-05: User retested deployed v0.9.77 at actual Chrome 200% zoom on the same 1920x1050 desktop. The off-canvas navigation opened and scrolled vertically to League Setup, League Setup was reachable and usable without observed clipping or horizontal page overflow, and a player-detail dialog remained readable, scrollable, and closeable at 200% zoom. The real-browser 200% critical workflow passed.
items.notes: Passed in the real deployed Chrome/Windows session at actual 200% zoom after v0.9.77. Automated reflow audits remain deterministic regression gates alongside this field evidence.

items.title: Representative physical phone workflow
evidence: 2026-09-05: User exercised the deployed site on a representative physical phone and confirmed the mobile workflow looked good across primary navigation, player detail, Waivers, Season Plan, and League Setup. No important clipping, overlap, or required horizontal page scrolling was reported, and the controls remained usable by touch.
items.notes: Representative physical-phone UI workflow passed. Encrypted cross-device sync lifecycle is tracked separately by FV-SYNC-01.

items.title: Authenticated standard ESPN league
items.notes: Validate connect, refresh, roster, matchup, lineup, waiver, change timeline, and Season Plan against a real standard-format league.

items.title: Authenticated custom FLEX or OP league
items.notes: Validate custom lineup slots, including FLEX/OP or superflex-style eligibility, without assuming unsupported slot mappings.

items.title: Authenticated acquisition and position limits
evidence: 2026-09-05: Live authenticated refresh reached ESPN roster settings but v0.9.72 rejected an unsupported roster position-limit id 6 before normalization. v0.9.73 adds fail-closed handling for unsupported unlimited/disabled limits.

2026-09-05: User retested the deployed v0.9.73 production site against the same authenticated ESPN league and confirmed Refresh ESPN completed successfully. Normalization compatibility is verified for this live roster-limit shape.

2026-09-05: User recording of League Setup after successful live refresh showed roster size 16; lineup slots QB 1, RB 2, WR 2, TE 1, D/ST 1, K 1, BE 6, IR 1, FLEX 1; finite position limits QB 4, RB 8, WR 8, TE 3, K 3, D/ST 3; season acquisition limit Unlimited; season acquisitions 0; weekly limit Unlimited; Week 1 acquisitions unavailable; waiver priority 10; processing days unavailable; budget remaining 100.

2026-09-05: Direct ESPN League Settings recording confirmed Roster Size 15, Total Starters 9, Total on Bench 6 (1 IR), and position maximums QB 4, RB 8, WR 8, TE 3, K 3, D/ST 3. ESPN acquisition settings showed Player Acquisition System Waivers, Season Acquisition Limit No Limit, Waiver Period 1 Day, and Waiver Order reset each week to inverse order of standings; the league does not use FAAB. Compared with v0.9.73 this exposed three parity defects: roster size displayed as 16, waiver period unavailable, and a phantom budget remaining 100.

2026-09-05: Deployed v0.9.74 League Setup retest matched the ESPN settings: roster size 15; finite position limits QB 4, RB 8, WR 8, TE 3, K 3, D/ST 3; player acquisition system Waivers; season and weekly limits Unlimited; waiver priority 10; waiver period 1 day; acquisition budget Not used. Week 1 acquisition usage remained unavailable rather than being inferred.

2026-09-05: Real Waivers-page recording after the v0.9.74 refresh reported no clear lineup upgrades and explicitly stated that ESPN-reported roster size and position limits were enforced and known ESPN acquisition limits and usage were checked before evaluating moves. The page retained waiver priority 10 while explicitly not predicting claim outcomes.
items.notes: Observed real ESPN acquisition settings, roster-size rules, provider-position limits, and waiver legality now match the ESPN-reported state for the tested authenticated league.

items.title: Authenticated IR edge states
items.notes: Observe supported eligible, grandfathered, filled, invalid, and/or unverified IR states as real league opportunities arise; never manufacture a live state.

items.title: Authenticated lock and availability transitions
items.notes: Observe at least one real game-lock or availability transition across refreshes and verify prior advice is revalidated or obsoleted correctly.

items.title: Real playoff and bye intelligence states
items.notes: Validate ESPN playoff-week boundaries or labeled local fallback, fantasy playoff opponents, bye coverage, and partial/full future projection behavior against real league state.

items.title: Live ESPN session or network refresh failure and reconnect
items.notes: Observe an actual expired-session, companion, ESPN service, or network failure; verify the last valid snapshot survives and reconnect/refresh guidance is accurate.

items.title: Live deployed sync revoke and delete
evidence: 2026-09-05: During real encrypted mobile-sync setup, the user reported that Refresh mobile data and Copy mobile link appeared to take a long time. Review found that successful sync actions disabled the initiating button but only restored it on error, so refresh/copy could remain visibly disabled until a later rerender; sync HTTP calls also lacked an explicit timeout.

2026-09-05: v0.9.78 candidate restores mounted sync buttons after both success and failure, provides explicit busy labels, and bounds publish/read/delete requests with an 8-second timeout. Automated unit/browser coverage verifies refresh and copy return to enabled state after success. Real deployed create/read/refresh/revoke/delete retest is still required before this item can pass.

2026-09-05: During the deployed v0.9.78 sync lifecycle retest, the private phone link loaded the correct ESPN league but opened a different league team than the desktop-selected team. Review reproduced the cause without retaining private league data: the encrypted sync payload omitted selectedTeamId, and a synced load therefore fell back to the first team in the snapshot.

2026-09-05: v0.9.79 candidate carries selectedTeamId inside the AES-256-GCM encrypted payload, validates that it belongs to the synced snapshot, and re-selects it immediately after mobile load. Regression coverage protects selected-team round-trip, invalid-team fail-closed behavior, legacy payload readability, and the mobile renderer's team-selection dispatch. Real deployed retest is still required before this item can pass.
items.notes: Pending deployed v0.9.79 mobile-sync lifecycle retest: confirm the phone opens the same desktop-selected team, refresh succeeds, revoke succeeds, and the revoked link no longer loads.

items.title: Real waiver candidate volume and timing
evidence: 2026-09-05: User recorded opening the real Waivers page after an authenticated v0.9.74 refresh and reported a small perceptible delay. Video review shows the transition from Overview to the rendered Waiver Wire completing within a few tenths of a second at 30 fps, with no visible long freeze or broken intermediate state. Candidate/scenario enumeration counts were not visible in this recording, so this performance item remains pending until those counts and timing are captured as projection coverage grows.

2026-09-05: v0.9.76 candidate adds runtime performance gates without a hidden candidate cap. GitHub Actions exhaustively evaluated 24 available adds x 4 unlocked bench drops (96 future scenarios) and measured 15.9 ms cold waiver analysis, 52.2 ms full priority-board evaluation after the waiver render, 0.6 ms playoff-only future baseline evaluation, and 37.0 ms repeat priority navigation on the CI runner. These deterministic measurements do not replace the required real deployed browser retest.

2026-09-05: After v0.9.76 was merged, deployed, and production-smoke verified, the user hard-refreshed the real app and confirmed the previously visible Waivers and Season Plan navigation lag is gone. This validates the responsiveness fix in the real browser; candidate/scenario enumeration counts are still required before this field item can pass.
items.notes: Real deployed v0.9.76 navigation responsiveness is confirmed fixed. Keep this item pending until consideredAdds, completeAdds, scenarioCount, and qualifiedAdds are captured as projection coverage grows. Do not introduce a hidden candidate cap.
